title: Type Ia supernova Hubble diagram: DES-SN5YR, 1,829 supernovae

object.name: Type Ia supernovae of the Dark Energy Survey five-year sample and its low-redshift companions
object.frame: redshift in the CMB frame; distance modulus on the release scale (H0 = 70)

facility.observatory: Dark Energy Survey (CTIO) with low-redshift supernovae from other surveys

columns.name: redshift
columns.description: zHD, the redshift corrected to the CMB frame and for peculiar velocity

columns.name: distance modulus
columns.description: MU, on the release's scale: H0 = 70 and its fixed absolute magnitude

columns.name: distance modulus error
columns.description: MUERR_FINAL, statistical, with the intrinsic scatter included

columns.name: survey
columns.description: 1 for a supernova found by the Dark Energy Survey, 0 for the low-redshift compilation

reductions: All 1,829 rows of DES-SN5YR_HD.csv, sorted by redshift (then identifier). The identifier, the CMB-frame and heliocentric redshifts are not kept; IDSURVEY is reduced to one flag (10 is the Dark Energy Survey).

Statistical errors only: the published cosmology uses the full systematic covariance matrix (16 MB compressed), which is not shipped, and the statistical covariance in the release is all zeros. A fit to this table is therefore not the published fit.
The distance moduli are on a scale fixed to H0 = 70 and the survey's absolute magnitude, so H0 is not measured by these supernovae alone: they fix the shape of the curve, not its scale.
75 of the 1,829 rows have an error above 1 mag (the largest 450): the survey's down-weighted candidates. They are kept, as the release keeps them, and carry almost no weight in a weighted fit.

Redshift is stored to 1e-5 and the modulus and its error to 1e-4 mag, the raw file's own digits: the mean redshift and mean modulus of the stored table equal the raw file's to better than 1e-12 relative (the manifest records the rounding).

citations.text: Sanchez et al. 2024 (The Dark Energy Survey Supernova Program: cosmological analysis and systematic uncertainties)
DES Collaboration 2024, ApJL 973, L14 (The Dark Energy Survey: cosmology results with ~1500 new high-redshift type Ia supernovae using the full 5-year dataset)

steps: Read zHD, MU, MUERR_FINAL and IDSURVEY from DES-SN5YR_HD.csv (the file as the zip holds it).
Sort by zHD, then by identifier.
Store redshift, modulus, error and the survey flag as table-columns/1.

assumptions: The errors are statistical and include an intrinsic-scatter term; they are treated as independent Gaussians.

The raw file is committed beside this tool (tools/data-packs/cosmology/DES-SN5YR_HD.csv, 91,860 bytes, CC BY 4.0, from the zip member named in the record): the zip is too large to fetch for a 92 KB table.

validation.check: a flat Lambda-CDM fit with the offset solved gives Omega_m within 0.08 of the published flat value 0.352 +- 0.017 (statistical errors only here, the full covariance there)
